issues: No sign of getting around the measurement: the noise augmentation touches only the training features (Dq). Test features (Dtq) are only transformed, and test labels are never used.

Not a bug, but worth noting: with early_stopping=True, MLPClassifier draws its validation split from the augmented set. Noisy copies of training rows can land in the validation split, so early stopping sees an optimistic score and may stop late. This affects the fit only, not the harness scoring.
Recomputed z = (0.0836 - 0.0825) / (0.0049 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2)) ≈ 0.0011 / 0.0060 ≈ 0.18. This matches the reported 0.180, and the gain is well within noise. Reject is the right call.
The change trains 3 MLPs on 3x the data, roughly 9x the MLP cost per fold. That adds complexity and runtime for a gain that is not significant, which the simplicity rule argues against.
